answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock scarce stake for a fixed period before its votes or work count, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves duplicate control or fabricated claims. A quill-signed audit record lets others verify the evidence, while a pulse of periodic checks keeps dormant farms from slipping through; velvet onboarding can make the delay feel gentle, but cannot waive the bond. A sybil attacker must tie up real capital in every persona and risks losing it, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free.
